newsitem.title: ITALY: Police scuffle with anti-Bossi protesters in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Police scuffle with anti-Bossi protesters in Italy.

text.p: Italian police used truncheons to beat back a group of extreme-rightists on a pro-unity march on Sunday when they tried to force their way through barricades, witnesses said.

A Reuters Television cameraman who filmed the incident in the Adriatic town of Chioggia at the south end of the Venice lagoon said the demonstrators had apparently wanted to reach a rally staged by separatist Umberto Bossi of the Northern League.

Some of the protesters, led by extreme-right southern politician Giancarlo Cito, were dressed in fascist-style black shirts. Several were struck by police truncheons but there were no serious injuries, cameraman Cristiano Corvino reported.
A police spokesman in the town described the incident as "scuffles" and said the situation was under control.
Bossi was leading a flotilla of boats on Sunday from Chioggia to Venice, where he planned to proclaim a "republic of Padania" covering Italy's affluent north.
His planned proclamation, the climax to a three-day "March to the Sea" along the River Po, has been matched by several counter-demonstrations throughout Italy, most of them peaceful.

In Turin, northwest Italy, several police and bystanders were slightly injured on Friday night when left-wing youths tried to storm League supporters and threw stones and bottles. Police used tear gas to restore order.
Cito, a former mayor of the southern city of Taranto, was elected to the national parliament last April on his own extreme-right ticket.
He reached Chioggia by rail several hours late on Sunday after a bomb hoax held up his train, railway officials said.
